arxiv-1507-04678.creator: Reinhard Kahle, Wilfried Keller
arxiv-1507-04678.description: Abstract We report on the idea to use colours to distinguish syntax and semantics as an educational tool in logic classes. This distinction gives also reason to reflect on some philosophical issues concerning semantics. 1]CMA and DM, FCT, Universidade Nova de Lisboa P-2829-526 Caparica, Portugal kahle@mat.uc.pt 2]Universität des Saarlandes 66123 Saarbrücken, Germany wilfried.keller@uni-saarland.de \serieslogo logo_ttl \volumeinfo M.

arxiv-2103-11426.title: Behavioural Movement Strategies in Cyclic Models
arxiv-2103-11426.creator: B. Moura, J. Menezes
arxiv-2103-11426.description: Abstract The spatial segregation of species is fundamental to ecosystem formation and stability. Behavioural strategies may determine where species are located and how their interactions change the local environment arrangement. In response to stimuli in the environment, individuals may move in a specific direction instead of walking randomly.

arxiv-2109-07078.title: DSOR: A Scalable Statistical Filter for Removing Falling Snow from LiDAR Point Clouds in Severe Winter Weather
arxiv-2109-07078.creator: Akhil Kurup, Jeremy Bos
arxiv-2109-07078.description: Abstract For autonomous vehicles to viably replace human drivers they must contend with inclement weather. Falling rain and snow introduce noise in LiDAR returns resulting in both false positive and false negative object detections. In this article we introduce the Winter Adverse Driving dataSet (WADS) collected in the snow belt region of Michigan’s Upper Peninsula.

arxiv-2109-10027.title: Endogenous Growth Under Multiple Uses of Data The authors thank Shota Ichihashi and Liyan Yang for helpful discussions and comments, as well as to the conference participants at the 2021 Conference on Markets and Economies with Information Frictions. Desheng Ma and Ramtin Salamat provided excellent
arxiv-2109-10027.creator: Lin William Cong, Wenshi Wei, Danxia Xie, Longtian Zhang
arxiv-2109-10027.description: Abstract We model a dynamic data economy with fully endogenous growth where agents generate data from consumption and share them with innovation and production firms. Different from other productive factors such as labor or capital, data are nonrival in their uses across sectors which affect both the level and growth of economic outputs.

arxiv-2206-02165.title: A Survey on Deep Learning based Channel Estimation in Doubly Dispersive Environments
arxiv-2206-02165.creator: Abdul Karim Gizzini, Marwa Chafii
arxiv-2206-02165.description: Abstract Wireless communications systems are impacted by multi-path fading and Doppler shift in dynamic environments, where the channel becomes doubly-dispersive and its estimation becomes an arduous task. Only a few pilots are used for channel estimation in conventional approaches to preserve high data rate transmission. Consequently, such estimators experience a significant performance degradation in high mobility scenarios.

arxiv-2304-09710.title: Complete λ \lambda -submanifolds in Gauss spaces
arxiv-2304-09710.creator: Doan The Hieu
arxiv-2304-09710.description: Abstract In this paper, we study λ \lambda -submanifolds of arbitrary codimensions in Gauss spaces. These submanifolds can be seen as natural generalizations of self-shrinker and λ \lambda -hypersurfaces. Using a divergence type theorem and some Simons’ type identities, we prove some halfspace type theorems and gap theorems for complete proper λ \lambda -submanifolds.

arxiv-2306-16868.title: Cosmology in Minkowski space
arxiv-2306-16868.creator: Lucas Lombriser
arxiv-2306-16868.description: Abstract Theoretical and observational challenges to standard cosmology such as the cosmological constant problem and tensions between cosmological model parameters inferred from different observations motivate the development and search of new physics. A less radical approach to venturing beyond the standard model is the simple mathematical reformulation of our theoretical frameworks underlying it.

arxiv-2308-15067.title: Probing Quarkyonic Matter in Neutron Stars with the Bayesian Nuclear-Physics Multi-Messenger Astrophysics Framework Preprint: LA-UR-23-29118

arxiv-2311-00706.title: Can AI Mitigate Human Perceptual Biases? A Pilot Study
arxiv-2311-00706.creator: Ross Geuy The Ohio State University, Nate Rising Carnegie Mellon University, Tiancheng Shi Columbia University, Meng Ling The Ohio State University and Shell plc, Jian Chen The Ohio State University
arxiv-2311-00706.description: Abstract We present results from a pilot experiment to measure if machine recommendations can debias human perceptual biases in visualization tasks. We specifically studied the “pull-down” effect, i.e., people underestimate the average position of lines [ 23 ] , for the task of estimating the ensemble average of data points in line charts.

arxiv-2407-04775.title: The first catalog of candidate white dwarf-main sequence binaries in open star clusters: A new window into common envelope evolution Facilities: Gaia, Gemini (GMOS), Kepler/K2, Lick (Kast), Pan-STARRS, TESS, ZTF, 2MASS astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ;

arxiv-2407-04775.description: Abstract Close binary systems are the progenitors to both Type Ia supernovae and the compact object mergers that can be detected via gravitational waves. To achieve a binary with a small radial separation, it is believed that the system likely undergoes common envelope (CE) evolution.

arxiv-2407-13717.creator: Usman Gohar, Michael C. Hunter, Robyn R. Lutz, Myra B. Cohen
arxiv-2407-13717.description: Abstract . Constructing assurance cases is a widely used, and sometimes required, process toward demonstrating that safety-critical systems will operate safely in their planned environment. To mitigate the risk of errors and missing edge cases, the concept of defeaters - arguments or evidence that challenge claims in an assurance case - has been introduced.

arxiv-2410-06733.title: Weak-eval-Strong: Evaluating and Eliciting Lateral Thinking of LLMs with Situation Puzzles
arxiv-2410-06733.creator: Qi Chen Bowen Zhang Gang Wang Qi Wu †
arxiv-2410-06733.description: Abstract While advancements in NLP have significantly improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on tasks requiring vertical thinking, their lateral thinking capabilities remain under-explored and challenging to measure due to the complexity of assessing creative thought processes and the scarcity of relevant data.

arxiv-2601-21727.title: Detection of hot subdwarf binaries and sdB stars using machine learning methods and a large sample of Gaia XP spectra
arxiv-2601-21727.creator: M. Ambrosch, C. Viscasillas Vázquez, E. Solano, A. Ulla, X. Pérez-Couto, E. Pérez-Fernández, A. Medžiūnas, M. Manteiga, C. Dafonte, A. Drazdauskas, L. Magrini, Š. Mikolaitis, V. Šatas
arxiv-2601-21727.description: Abstract Context. Hot subdwarfs (hot sds) are compact, evolved stars near the Extreme Horizontal Branch (EHB), key to understanding stellar evolution and the UV excess in galaxies. We extend our previous analysis of Gaia XP spectra of hot subdwarf stars to a much larger sample, enabling a comprehensive study of their physical and binary properties. Aims.

pmc-11300967.title: Exploring the facilitators and barriers to addressing social media’s impact on anxiety within primary care: a qualitative study
pmc-11300967.creator: Ailin Anto, Rafey Omar Asif, Arunima Basu, Dylan Kanapathipillai, Haadi Salam, Rania Selim, Jahed Zaman, Andreas Benedikt Eisingerich
pmc-11300967.description: BackgroundSeveral researchers and policymakers have acknowledged the alarming association between social media (SM) usage and anxiety symptoms in young adults. While primary care holds a crucial role in the improvement of health outcomes for those presenting with anxiety, there has been no research on GPs’ perceptions of the impact of SM on anxiety.

pmc-11461022.title: Genetic Structure of Monochamus alternatus (Hope) in Qinling‐Daba Mountains and Expansion Trend: Implications for Pest Prevention and Management

pmc-11461022.description: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus, severely threatens global pine forests. Monochamus alternatus is the primary vector of B. xylophilus in East Asia. Understanding the population structure and evolutionary forces of vector insects is critical for establishing effective PWD management strategies. The present work explores the genetic structure and phylogenetic relationships of 20 populations of M.

pmc-13183144.title: Development and validation of a predictive model for early postoperative pain after cesarean section
pmc-13183144.creator: Pu Xu, Hui Huang, Guangyin Qiu, Hui Cheng, Li Feng
pmc-13183144.description: This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for early postoperative pain following cesarean section and to develop a reliable nomogram prediction model to facilitate clinical risk assessment and individualized pain management. We retrospectively collected clinical data from women who underwent cesarean section at our hospital between January 2022 and December 2023.

pmc-13345593.title: Case Report: High-dose pregabalin ingestion in an adolescent: clinical course and serial plasma concentrations
pmc-13345593.creator: Raffaele Simeoli, Enrico Armiento, Sara Cairoli, Mara Pisani, Paola Silvestri, Marco Marano
pmc-13345593.description: BackgroundPregabalin (PGB) is widely used for neuropathic pain, generalized anxiety disorder, and seizure management; however, recent epidemiological data highlight a progressive increase in its misuse and involvement in intoxications, particularly among adolescents and individuals with psychiatric comorbidities. Although dose–toxicity relationships have been explored in adult populations, substantial interindividual variability persists, and data in pediatric or adolescent patients remain limited.

pmc-13445804.title: Private garden exposure and public park access in relation to type-2 diabetes incidence: a UK Biobank cohort study
pmc-13445804.creator: Chinonso Christian Odebeatu, Darsy Darssan, Charlotte Roscoe, Simon Reid, Nicholas J Osborne
pmc-13445804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundExisting longitudinal studies examining the relationship between greenspace exposure and incidence of type-2 diabetes (T2D) have primarily operationalized greenspace using vegetation indices. Little is known about the effect of greenspace types (e.g., private gardens) and public park access.MethodsWe investigated the associations between residential greenspace exposure, including private gardens (determined using Ordnance Survey MasterMap™ Greenspace) and public park access, with the incidence of T2D using the UK Biobank (UKBB) data.
